title: AAPS+Nightscout for selfhosting (SSL)
symptom: AndroidAPS requires an SSL connection to Nightscout, but the user wants to self-host Nightscout privately on a VPN without public exposure. The user tried engineering_mode but still gets the error 'NS URL not encrypted', and Nightscout lacks full authentication for its web frontend, so they are reluctant to expose it publicly.
cause: AndroidAPS does not allow unencrypted or self-signed certificate connections to Nightscout, and Nightscout's web frontend does not provide full authentication, preventing secure public exposure via reverse proxy.
fix: Use a newer Nightscout version (e.g. niepi/cgm-remote-monitor:14.0.7) that requires authentication even for viewing the web frontend, then expose the Nightscout site to the internet using HTTPS via a reverse proxy such as Caddy.
evidence_quote: OK, I made it working with the latest NS version (I used niepi/cgm-remote-monitor:14.0.7), there one needs to authenticate even for viewing the web frontend. With this I was able to open the site to the Internet.
